title: YouTube in AI search: see which channels, videos and moments AI cites
summary: AthenaHQ now breaks YouTube citations down by channel, video category, length, and the exact moment in a video that an AI answer links to.
body_markdown:
YouTube is one of the domains AI answers cite most. But a citation that says “youtube.com” doesn’t tell you much. You can’t brief a content team on it, and you can’t pick a creator to partner with from it.


AthenaHQ now opens up the YouTube source. For every video AI answers cite, you can see the channel that published it, its YouTube category, its length, and the moment in the video the answer pointed to.


## Which channels own the videos AI cites


The new Channels tab groups every cited video under the channel that published it.


- **Share of YouTube citations** for each channel, across every video of theirs that AI answers cited.
- **Expand a channel** to see its cited videos, with each video’s title, publish date, length and citations.
- **Filter by category and length** to narrow the list to, say, Education videos under five minutes.


**Why it matters:** a citation only becomes something you can act on once it has a name attached. If it’s your own channel, you know what to keep making. If it’s a creator, that’s a partnership shortlist. If it’s a competitor’s channel, that’s a gap with a name.


## What kind of videos get cited


The YouTube source’s Overview now shows how citations split by YouTube category and by video length. It also shows the median length of a cited video and the top channels.


**Why it matters:** “make more video” isn’t a plan. Knowing whether AI answers in your category cite two-minute explainers or forty-minute walkthroughs tells your team what to produce next.


## The exact moment AI points to


Some AI answers don’t just cite a video. They link to a specific second of it with a timestamp (` &t=` ). In the 30 days to October 29, 2026, across more than 420,000 YouTube citations AthenaHQ tracked:


- **Google AI Overviews** linked to a specific moment in **50%** of their YouTube citations.
- **Google AI Mode** did so in **47%** .
- **Grok** did so in **0.2%** , and ChatGPT, Perplexity, Gemini, Claude and Copilot never did.


The Timestamps tab shows how often each platform does this for your prompts, and lists every cited moment of every video with how often it was cited. Select a moment to open the video right there.


**Why it matters:** when Google cites a moment, that moment is the answer, not the video as a whole. If the cited moment is thirty seconds into a ten-minute video, those thirty seconds are what earned the citation. Clear chapters, a first sentence that answers the question, and an accurate transcript make those moments easier to find and quote.


## Get started


Open Sources in AthenaHQ, select youtube.com, and switch to the Channels or Timestamps tab. Both export to CSV, so the channel list or the cited moments can go straight into a content brief.


[See your YouTube citations in AthenaHQ](https://athenahq.ai/demo) , or ask us for a walkthrough with your own data.
